425	      grep -E '^ +(GAP|the previous session|log gap)' "$LIVE/bootstrap-hook.log" | sed -E 's/^ +/  - /' | tail -4
426	      echo "  LFS binaries: $(git lfs ls-files | awk '$2=="-"' | wc -l) pointer stubs left (0 = all restored)"
427	      echo "  Full bootstrap (tools, Blender, Android SDK, Marble, tests, autosave) is running in the background:"
428	      echo "  'bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --status' -> backups/BOOTSTRAP_REPORT.md. Read CLAUDE.md and"
429	      echo "  backups/CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_TRANSFER.md, then give the user the backup report described in CLAUDE.md."
430	    else
431	      echo "Rainbow: a bootstrap run is already in progress (backups/.live/bootstrap.log)."
432	    fi
433	  else
434	    bash scripts/install-autosave-scheduler.sh > "$HOME/.rainbow-autosave-install.log" 2>&1
435	    echo "Rainbow ($src): autosave re-armed. $(python3 -I scripts/autosave-status.py 2>&1 | head -1)"
436	  fi
437	  exit 0 ;;
438	
439	env-setup)   # cloud environment setup script: tools only, before Claude starts; never touches git; never fails
440	  : > "$RES"
441	  say "Rainbow env-setup: tools ($ROOT)"
442	  start_tool_installs
443	  step_node; step_npm; step_pylibs; step_playwright; step_media_tools; step_blender; step_android
444	  command -v claude >/dev/null && step_worldlabs
445	  exit 0 ;;
446	esac
447	
448	# full / check / background
449	exec 8>"$LIVE/bootstrap.lock"
450	if ! flock -w 600 8; then echo "another bootstrap run holds the lock (backups/.live/bootstrap.log)"; exit 1; fi
451	[ "$MODE" = background ] && renice -n 10 $$ >/dev/null 2>&1
452	echo "RAINBOW BOOTSTRAP ($MODE) $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC') - $ROOT"
453	if [ "$CONTINUE" = 0 ]; then
454	  : > "$RES"
455	  say "1 Repository, newest work, backup gap"
456	  step_identity
457	  step_resume
458	  if [ "$DO_RESUME" = 1 ] && ! cmp -s "$SELF" "$ROOT/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh"; then
459	    echo "      the merge brought a newer claude-bootstrap.sh: continuing with it"
460	    flock -u 8; exec 8>&-
461	    exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" "${ORIG_ARGS[@]}" --continue
462	  fi
463	fi
464	# after the merge, so an old checkout already has scripts/verify-assets.py (the hook ran this itself)
465	[ "$MODE" = background ] || pycheck gap "Backup gap since last session" gap --session-start "$(session_start)"
466	start_tool_installs
467	say "2 Game files: LFS binaries, references, screens, agents, Marble"
468	step_lfs
469	if [ "$FULL_TESTS" = 1 ]; then pycheck lfs_remote "Git LFS on GitHub" lfs-remote --download
470	else pycheck lfs_remote "Git LFS on GitHub" lfs-remote; fi
471	step_refs
472	step_screens
473	pycheck agents "Specialist agents" agents
474	pycheck marble "Marble World Labs assets" marble
475	step_worldlabs
476	say "3 Tools (installed only when missing)"
477	step_node; step_npm; step_pylibs; step_playwright; step_media_tools; step_blender; step_android
478	step_claude_config
479	say "4 Tests"
480	step_tests
481	if [ "$NO_AUTOSAVE" = 1 ]; then rec autosave "Five-minute GitHub autosave" skip "--no-autosave: scheduler not touched, nothing pushed" "$(now)"
482	elif [ "$MODE" != check ]; then say "5 Five-minute autosave"; step_autosave
483	else
484	  t=$(now); out="$(python3 -I scripts/autosave-status.py 2>&1)"; rc=$?
485	  rec autosave "Five-minute GitHub autosave" "$([ "$rc" = 0 ] && echo ok || echo warn)" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")" "$t"
486	fi
487	finish_report
488	[ "$FAILS" = 0 ]
489

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RAINBOW — one-command recovery + environment bootstrap for a new Claude account or cloud session.
# Safe to run any number of times: every step checks first and only installs / merges what is missing.
#
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh            full: resume newest work, LFS, refs, agents, Marble, tools, tests,
#                                               five-minute autosave, report (backups/BOOTSTRAP_REPORT.md)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --check    report only: no installs, no merges (fetch is still done)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --full     full + browser gameplay test + Screen 05 BEFORE pixel check
#                                               + fresh download of every LFS object from GitHub (SHA-256)
#   bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --status   last report + autosave verdict (instant)
#   options: --no-tools (skip Blender/Android/pip/plugin installs)  --skip-resume (no fetch/merge)
#   internal: --hook (SessionStart hook)  --background (rest of the hook run)  --env-setup (cloud setup script)
#
# New account, any start branch (the GitHub default branch is an OLD version):
#   git fetch origin <newest-branch> && git show FETCH_HEAD:scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh > /tmp/b.sh && bash /tmp/b.sh
#
# Safety: never force-pushes, resets, rebases, deletes files or rewrites history. Merges are normal merge commits;
# a merge that conflicts (outside auto-generated status files) is ABORTED and reported, never left half-done.
# Never pushes to backups/autosave.config.json -> protected_branches. Never reads, prints or stores credentials.
# Paid World Labs / Marble jobs are never started (only the free credit-balance read).
set -uo pipefail
ORIG_ARGS=("$@")
MODE=full; DO_RESUME=1; DO_TOOLS=1; FULL_TESTS=0; CONTINUE=0; NO_AUTOSAVE=0
UNSHALLOW_TIMEOUT=300; FETCH_TIMEOUT=180   # the SessionStart hook uses shorter limits
for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in
  --check) MODE=check; DO_RESUME=0; DO_TOOLS=0 ;;
  --full) FULL_TESTS=1 ;;
  --status) MODE=status ;;
  --hook) MODE=hook ;;
  --background) MODE=background; DO_RESUME=0; CONTINUE=1 ;;
  --env-setup) MODE=env-setup; DO_RESUME=0 ;;
  --no-tools|--skip-tools) DO_TOOLS=0 ;;
  --skip-resume) DO_RESUME=0 ;;
  --no-autosave) NO_AUTOSAVE=1 ;;   # tests in a throw-away clone: never install the scheduler or push
  --continue) CONTINUE=1; DO_RESUME=0 ;;
  --tools) ;;   # legacy flag of resume-newest-work.sh: tools are installed by default now
  -h|--help) sed -n '2,22p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; exit 0 ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $a (see --help)"; exit 2 ;;
esac; done
SELF="$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
REPO_SLUG="josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-"

find_root() {
  local d
  for d in "${RAINBOW_ROOT:-}" "$(cd "$(dirname "$SELF")/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)" "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" \
           "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" "$PWD/rainbow-" "/home/user/rainbow-"; do
    [ -n "$d" ] && [ -d "$d/.git" ] && git -C "$d" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$REPO_SLUG" \
      && { echo "$d"; return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
ROOT="$(find_root)" || { echo "claude-bootstrap: no checkout of $REPO_SLUG found (cd into it or set RAINBOW_ROOT)"; \
  [ "$MODE" = hook ] || [ "$MODE" = env-setup ] && exit 0; exit 1; }
cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
LIVE="$ROOT/backups/.live"; mkdir -p "$LIVE"
RES="$LIVE/bootstrap-results.jsonl"
SS_DIR="$HOME/.rainbow-bootstrap"; mkdir -p "$SS_DIR"
LFS_ACCESS_KEY="[REDACTED]"
FAILS=0

now() { date +%s; }
manifest() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
for k in sys.argv[2].split("."): d=d[k]
print(" ".join(d) if isinstance(d,list) else d)' "$ROOT/backups/TOOL_MANIFEST.json" "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
rec() {  # id title status(ok|warn|fail|skip) summary start_epoch
  local secs=$(( $(now) - ${5:-$(now)} ))
  python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"id":sys.argv[1],"title":sys.argv[2],"status":sys.argv[3],"summary":sys.argv[4],"seconds":int(sys.argv[5])}))' \
    "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$secs" >> "$RES"
  printf '  %-4s %-30s %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$3" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')" "$2" "$4"
  [ "$3" = fail ] && FAILS=$((FAILS + 1))
  return 0
}
pycheck() {  # id title verify-assets.py-args...
  local id="$1" title="$2" t out last st sm; shift 2; t=$(now)
  out="$(timeout 1200 python3 -I "$ROOT/scripts/verify-assets.py" "$@" 2>&1)"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^@@ ' | sed 's/^/      /'
  last="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep '^@@ ' | tail -1)"
  if [ -n "$last" ]; then st="$(cut -d' ' -f2 <<<"$last")"; sm="$(cut -d' ' -f3- <<<"$last")"
  else st=fail; sm="check crashed: $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1 | cut -c1-160)"; fi
  rec "$id" "$title" "$st" "$sm" "$t"
}
say() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
session_start() {
  if [ -s "$SS_DIR/session-start" ]; then cat "$SS_DIR/session-start"
  else date -u -d "$(ps -o lstart= -p 1 2>/dev/null)" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00 2>/dev/null || date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00; fi
}
autosave_lock() { exec 9>"$ROOT/backups/.autosave.lock"; flock -w "${1:-120}" 9; }
autosave_unlock() { flock -u 9 2>/dev/null; exec 9>&- 2>/dev/null; return 0; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- steps
step_identity() {
  local t branch prot; t=$(now)
  branch="$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '(detached)')"
  prot="$(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; c=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); print("yes" if sys.argv[2] in c.get("protected_branches",[]) else "no")' \
          "$ROOT/backups/autosave.config.json" "$branch" 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ "$prot" = yes ]; then
    rec identity "Repository + branch" fail "on PROTECTED branch $branch: the autosave refuses to push here. Start a new Claude session (it gets a new ccr-*/claude/* branch)" "$t"
  elif [[ "$branch" != ccr-* && "$branch" != claude/* ]]; then
    rec identity "Repository + branch" warn "branch $branch is not a ccr-*/claude/* session branch: the autosave will not push it" "$t"
  else
    rec identity "Repository + branch" ok "$REPO_SLUG on $branch @ $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) (session started from ${CLAUDE_CODE_BASE_REF:-unknown})" "$t"
  fi
}

AUTO_THEIRS=" backups/MANIFEST.json backups/BACKUP_STATUS.json backups/CONVERSATION_INDEX.md qa/capture_log.json backups/BOOTSTRAP_REPORT.md "
AUTO_UNION=" backups/BACKUP_LOG.md "
merge_one() {  # ref -> 0 merged | 1 conflict (aborted) | 2 refused
  local ref="$1" f tmpd
  if git merge --no-edit -q -m "resume: merge newer saved work from ${ref#origin/}" "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  if [ ! -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ]; then   # refused before starting (e.g. signing helper): retry unsigned once
    git -c commit.gpgsign=false merge --no-edit -q -m "resume: merge newer saved work from ${ref#origin/}" "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    [ -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ] || return 2
  fi
  tmpd="$(mktemp -d)"
  for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U); do
    if [[ "$AUTO_THEIRS" == *" $f "* ]]; then git checkout --theirs -- "$f" && git add -- "$f"
    elif [[ "$AUTO_UNION" == *" $f "* ]]; then
      git show ":2:$f" > "$tmpd/o"; git show ":1:$f" > "$tmpd/b" 2>/dev/null || : > "$tmpd/b"; git show ":3:$f" > "$tmpd/t"
      git merge-file --union "$tmpd/o" "$tmpd/b" "$tmpd/t"; cp "$tmpd/o" "$f"; git add -- "$f"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmpd"
  if [ -n "$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U)" ]; then
    CONFLICT_FILES="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | head -6 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    git merge --abort; return 1
  fi
  git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q --no-edit && return 0
  git merge --abort 2>/dev/null; return 2
}

step_resume() {
  local t merged="" conflicts="" refused="" total=0 contained=0 dirty ref; t=$(now)
  if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; then
    timeout "$UNSHALLOW_TIMEOUT" git fetch -q --unshallow origin 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if ! timeout "$FETCH_TIMEOUT" git fetch -q origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' 2>/dev/null; then
    rec resume "Resume newest work" fail "git fetch from GitHub failed (network / GitHub connection?)" "$t"; return
  fi
  if [ "$DO_RESUME" = 1 ]; then
    for busy in MERGE_HEAD rebase-merge rebase-apply CHERRY_PICK_HEAD; do
      [ -e ".git/$busy" ] && { rec resume "Resume newest work" fail "a git $busy is in progress: finish it first, then rerun" "$t"; return; }
    done
    dirty=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no | wc -l)
    if [ "$dirty" != 0 ]; then   # save the current edits first, so a merge can never touch unsaved work
      timeout 600 python3 "$ROOT/scripts/rainbow-autosave.py" --reason bootstrap:pre-merge --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1
      dirty=$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no | wc -l)
    fi
    if [ "$dirty" != 0 ]; then
      echo "      $dirty uncommitted tracked file(s) could not be saved first: not merging"
    elif autosave_lock 180; then
      for ref in $(git for-each-ref --sort=committerdate --format='%(refname:short)' refs/remotes/origin/ | grep -E '^origin/(ccr-|claude/)'); do
        git merge-base --is-ancestor "$ref" HEAD 2>/dev/null && continue
        echo "      merging $ref ($(git rev-parse --short "$ref"), $(git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format:'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' "$ref"))"
        CONFLICT_FILES=""
        merge_one "$ref"; case $? in
          0) merged="$merged ${ref#origin/}" ;;
          1) conflicts="$conflicts ${ref#origin/}[$CONFLICT_FILES]" ;;
          *) refused="$refused ${ref#origin/}" ;;
        esac
      done
      autosave_unlock
    else
      echo "      autosave lock busy for 3 min: not merging this time"
    fi
  fi
  for ref in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/remotes/origin/ | grep -E '^origin/(ccr-|claude/)'); do
    total=$((total + 1)); git merge-base --is-ancestor "$ref" HEAD 2>/dev/null && contained=$((contained + 1))
  done
  local msg head; head="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
  msg="$contained/$total remote ccr-*/claude/* branches contained in HEAD $head"
  [ -n "$merged" ] && msg="$msg; merged newer work from:$merged"
  if [ -n "$conflicts" ]; then
    rec resume "Resume newest work" fail "$msg; CONFLICT (merge aborted, nothing changed):$conflicts - merge by hand keeping both sides: git merge origin/<branch>" "$t"
  elif [ -n "$refused" ]; then
    rec resume "Resume newest work" fail "$msg; merge refused for:$refused (see git status)" "$t"
  elif [ "$contained" != "$total" ]; then
    rec resume "Resume newest work" warn "$msg; not merged ($([ "$DO_RESUME" = 1 ] && echo 'unsaved edits or busy lock' || echo 'check mode')): run bash scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" "$t"
  else
    rec resume "Resume newest work" ok "$msg" "$t"
  fi
}

lfs_pull() {  # bounded; holds the autosave lock so a backup never races the index update
  git config --unset-all "$LFS_ACCESS_KEY" 2>/dev/null
  git lfs install --local >/dev/null 2>&1
  [ "$(git lfs ls-files | awk '$2=="-"' | wc -l)" = 0 ] && return 0
  autosave_lock 120 || true
  timeout "${1:-600}" git lfs pull > "$LIVE/lfs-pull.log" 2>&1; local rc=$?
  autosave_unlock; return $rc
}

step_lfs() {
  local t stubs total; t=$(now)
  [ "$MODE" != check ] && lfs_pull 900
  total=$(git lfs ls-files | wc -l); stubs=$(git lfs ls-files | awk '$2=="-"' | wc -l)
  if [ "$stubs" != 0 ]; then
    rec lfs "Git LFS binaries (local)" fail "$stubs of $total LFS files are still pointer stubs ($( [ "$MODE" = check ] && echo 'check mode: run without --check' || echo "see backups/.live/lfs-pull.log"))" "$t"
  elif git lfs fsck >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rec lfs "Git LFS binaries (local)" ok "$total/$total real files (models, APK, kit ZIP, Marble splats/PLY/colliders/.blend), git lfs fsck OK" "$t"
  else
    rec lfs "Git LFS binaries (local)" fail "git lfs fsck reported problems (run: git lfs fsck)" "$t"
  fi
}

step_refs() {
  local t n okc; t=$(now)
  n=$(grep -c . scripts/reference.sha256); okc=$(sha256sum -c scripts/reference.sha256 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': OK$')
  if [ "$okc" = "$n" ]; then rec refs "Approved references" ok "$okc/$n byte-identical (scripts/reference.sha256, incl. the official cartoon-girl reference)" "$t"
  else rec refs "Approved references" fail "only $okc/$n match scripts/reference.sha256 - restore them from git, never edit" "$t"; fi
}

step_screens() {
  local t n=0 f; t=$(now)
  for f in references/0[1-9]_*.png references/1[01]_*.png; do [ -f "$f" ] && n=$((n + 1)); done
  if [ "$n" -ge 11 ] && [ -f src/main.ts ] && [ -d src ]; then
    rec screens "Game: 11 screens + code" ok "$n approved screen references 01-11, source tree src/ ($(git ls-files src | wc -l) files), Android project android/, characters assets/models/*.glb" "$t"
  else rec screens "Game: 11 screens + code" fail "expected 11 references (01-11) and src/main.ts; found $n" "$t"; fi
}

step_worldlabs() {
  local t out key plugin st=ok; t=$(now)
  # free reads only; only HTTP 401/403 means "reconnect the key via the secure form" (never ask otherwise)
  out="$(timeout 120 python3 -I scripts/verify-assets.py worldlabs 2>/dev/null | grep '^@@ ' | tail -1)"
  key="$(cut -d' ' -f3- <<<"$out")"; [ -n "$key" ] || key="Marble API check did not run"
  case "$(cut -d' ' -f2 <<<"$out")" in ok) ;; *) st=warn ;; esac
  if timeout 60 claude plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'worldlabs@'; then plugin="installed"
  elif [ "$DO_TOOLS" = 1 ] && command -v claude >/dev/null; then
    bash scripts/setup-worldlabs-plugin.sh > "$LIVE/worldlabs-plugin.log" 2>&1
    timeout 60 claude plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'worldlabs@' && plugin="installed now" || { plugin="install FAILED (backups/.live/worldlabs-plugin.log)"; st=warn; }
  else plugin="not installed (bash scripts/setup-worldlabs-plugin.sh)"; st=warn; fi
  rec worldlabs "World Labs integration" "$st" "$key; plugin worldlabs@worldlabs $plugin; Atlas connector = claude.ai connector (check in Claude: ToolSearch World_Labs_Atlas); no paid job started" "$t"
}

step_node() {
  local t v; t=$(now); v="$(node -v 2>/dev/null)"
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^v([0-9]+) ]] && [ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" -ge 20 ]; then rec node "Node.js" ok "$v, npm $(npm -v 2>/dev/null)" "$t"
  else rec node "Node.js" fail "need Node >= 20, found ${v:-none}" "$t"; fi
}

step_npm() {
  local t h=node_modules/.rainbow-bootstrap.sha256; t=$(now)
  if sha256sum --check --status "$h" 2>/dev/null && [ -d node_modules/three ] && [ -d node_modules/vite ]; then
    rec npm "npm dependencies" ok "node_modules up to date with package-lock.json (npm ci skipped)" "$t"; return
  fi
  if [ "$MODE" = check ]; then rec npm "npm dependencies" warn "node_modules missing or stale (run without --check)" "$t"; return; fi
  rm -f "$h"
  if timeout 900 npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --prefer-offline > "$LIVE/npm-ci.log" 2>&1; then
    sha256sum package.json package-lock.json > "$h"
    rec npm "npm dependencies" ok "npm ci done ($(ls node_modules | wc -l) packages; cache ~/.npm reused)" "$t"
  else rec npm "npm dependencies" fail "npm ci failed (backups/.live/npm-ci.log)" "$t"; fi
}

py_missing() { python3 -I -c 'import importlib.util as u,sys; print(" ".join(m for m in sys.argv[1:] if u.find_spec(m) is None))' "$@"; }
step_pylibs() {
  local t req opt mreq mopt pkgs="" m st=ok msg; t=$(now)
  req="numpy PIL"; opt="cv2 scipy"
  mreq="$(py_missing $req)"; mopt="$(py_missing $opt)"
  if [ -n "$mreq$mopt" ] && [ "$DO_TOOLS" = 1 ]; then
    for m in $mreq $mopt; do case $m in PIL) pkgs="$pkgs Pillow";; cv2) pkgs="$pkgs opencv-python-headless";; *) pkgs="$pkgs $m";; esac; done
    timeout 600 python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check $pkgs > "$LIVE/pip.log" 2>&1 \
      || timeout 600 python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --break-system-packages $pkgs >> "$LIVE/pip.log" 2>&1
    mreq="$(py_missing $req)"; mopt="$(py_missing $opt)"
    msg="installed:$pkgs; "
  fi
  [ -n "$mopt" ] && st=warn
  [ -n "$mreq" ] && st=fail
  rec pylibs "Python QA libraries" "$st" "${msg:-}$(python3 --version 2>&1); required numpy+Pillow $([ -z "$mreq" ] && echo OK || echo "MISSING: $mreq"); optional cv2+scipy $([ -z "$mopt" ] && echo OK || echo "missing: $mopt")" "$t"
}

step_playwright() {
  local t out; t=$(now)
  out="$(timeout 120 node scripts/lib/pw-smoke.mjs 2>&1 | tail -1)"
  if grep -q '"ok":true' <<<"$out"; then
    rec playwright "Playwright + Chromium" ok "headless Chromium $(sed -E 's/.*"chromium":"([^"]+)".*/\1/' <<<"$out") with WebGL2 (SwiftShader); preinstalled, never reinstall" "$t"
  else rec playwright "Playwright + Chromium" fail "smoke test failed: ${out:0:160}" "$t"; fi
}

blender_ok() { blender --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q "Blender $(manifest tools.blender.version)"; }
android_ok() { local s=/opt/android-sdk; [ -d "$s/platforms/android-34" ] && [ -x "$s/build-tools/34.0.0/aapt2" ] && [ -x "$s/platform-tools/adb" ]; }
start_tool_installs() {  # Blender + Android SDK downloads run in parallel, in the background
  BL_PID=""; AN_PID=""
  [ "$DO_TOOLS" = 1 ] || return 0
  if ! blender_ok; then
    ( BLENDER_VERSION="$(manifest tools.blender.version)" bash scripts/setup-blender.sh > "$LIVE/blender-setup.log" 2>&1 ) & BL_PID=$!
  fi
  if ! android_ok; then ( bash scripts/setup-android-sdk.sh > "$LIVE/android-setup.log" 2>&1 ) & AN_PID=$!; fi
}

step_blender() {
  local t was=present v; t=$(now)
  [ -n "${BL_PID:-}" ] && { wait "$BL_PID"; was="installed now"; }
  if blender_ok; then
    v="$(blender --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
    if timeout 180 blender -b --factory-startup --python-expr "import bpy; print('BPY_OK', bpy.app.version_string)" 2>/dev/null | grep -q BPY_OK; then
      rec blender "Blender" ok "$v ($was) at $(command -v blender); headless bpy test OK" "$t"
    else rec blender "Blender" fail "$v installed but the headless bpy test failed" "$t"; fi
  elif [ "$DO_TOOLS" = 1 ]; then rec blender "Blender" fail "install failed (needs download.blender.org) - backups/.live/blender-setup.log" "$t"
  else rec blender "Blender" warn "Blender $(manifest tools.blender.version) not installed (run without --check / --no-tools)" "$t"; fi
}

step_android() {
  local t was=present jv sdk=/opt/android-sdk; t=$(now)
  [ -n "${AN_PID:-}" ] && { wait "$AN_PID"; was="installed now"; }
  jv="$(java -version 2>&1 | grep -v JAVA_TOOL | grep -oE 'version "[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')"
  if android_ok; then
    if [ ! -f android/local.properties ] || ! grep -q "^sdk.dir=$sdk$" android/local.properties; then
      echo "sdk.dir=$sdk" > android/local.properties   # git-ignored
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code hook entry point:  autosave-hook.sh <SessionStart|PreCompact|Stop|SessionEnd>
# SessionStart -> scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --hook: merges newer saved work, restores Git LFS, re-arms the
#   five-minute autosave, prints a short recovery summary for Claude and runs the full bootstrap in the background.
# Stop runs in the background so it never delays a turn (and re-arms the scheduler if it died);
# PreCompact/SessionEnd run one verified autosave inline (bounded).
EVENT="${1:-hook}"
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
case "$EVENT" in
  SessionStart)
    if [ -f "$REPO/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" ]; then
      exec bash "$REPO/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh" --hook     # reads the hook JSON (source) from stdin
    fi
    # fallback for an old checkout without the bootstrap
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    bash "$REPO/scripts/install-autosave-scheduler.sh" > "$HOME/.rainbow-autosave-install.log" 2>&1
    git -C "$REPO" config --unset-all "lfs.https://github.com/josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-.git/info/lfs.access" 2>/dev/null
    setsid nohup bash -c "timeout 240 git -C '$REPO' lfs pull >'$HOME/.rainbow-lfs-pull.log' 2>&1; \
      '$REPO/scripts/autosave-cron.sh' hook:SessionStart" >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    ;;
  Stop)
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    bash "$REPO/scripts/install-autosave-scheduler.sh" > "$HOME/.rainbow-autosave-install.log" 2>&1
    setsid nohup "$REPO/scripts/autosave-cron.sh" "hook:Stop" >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    ;;
  PreCompact|SessionEnd)
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 110 "$REPO/scripts/autosave-cron.sh" "hook:$EVENT" >/dev/null 2>&1
    ;;
  *)
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    ;;
esac
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs (idempotently) the Rainbow five-minute autosave scheduler on this machine.
#   * Linux with cron  -> crontab entry  */5 * * * *  + starts the cron daemon if it is not running
#   * no cron available -> falls back to a detached loop daemon (scripts/autosave-daemon.sh)
# Session env needed by git (proxy, CA bundle, url rewrites) is captured to ~/.rainbow-autosave.env
# (chmod 600, outside the repo; it contains NO tokens — auth is handled by the git proxy/helper).
set -u
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ENVF="$HOME/.rainbow-autosave.env"
LOGD="$HOME/.rainbow-autosave"
mkdir -p "$LOGD"

# 1. capture non-secret environment that git/curl need outside the interactive session
{
  echo "# generated by install-autosave-scheduler.sh — proxy/CA/git-url settings only"
  for v in PATH HOME HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy SSL_CERT_FILE \
           CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE GIT_SSL_CAINFO NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT \
           GIT_EDITOR GIT_CONFIG_COUNT CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID; do
    [ -n "${!v-}" ] && printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$v" "${!v}"
  done
  n="${GIT_CONFIG_COUNT:-0}"
  for ((i=0; i<n; i++)); do
    k="GIT_CONFIG_KEY_$i"; val="GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_$i"
    printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$k" "${!k-}"
    printf 'export %s=%q\n' "$val" "${!val-}"
  done
} > "$ENVF"
chmod 600 "$ENVF"

RUNNER="$REPO/scripts/autosave-cron.sh"
chmod +x "$RUNNER" "$REPO/scripts/autosave-daemon.sh" "$REPO/scripts/rainbow-autosave.py" 2>/dev/null

if command -v crontab >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v cron >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  LINE="*/5 * * * * $RUNNER cron >> $LOGD/cron.log 2>&1 # rainbow-autosave"
  ( crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v '# rainbow-autosave' ; echo "$LINE" ) | crontab -
  if ! pgrep -x cron >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    cron 2>/dev/null || /usr/sbin/cron 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if pgrep -x cron >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "scheduler=cron status=active entry='$LINE'"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "cron daemon could not start; falling back to loop daemon" >&2
fi

# fallback: detached loop daemon with pidfile
PIDF="$LOGD/daemon.pid"
if [ -f "$PIDF" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDF")" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "scheduler=daemon status=active pid=$(cat "$PIDF")"
  exit 0
fi
setsid nohup "$REPO/scripts/autosave-daemon.sh" >> "$LOGD/daemon.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
echo $! > "$PIDF"
echo "scheduler=daemon status=started pid=$(cat "$PIDF")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code hook entry point:  autosave-hook.sh <SessionStart|PreCompact|Stop|SessionEnd>
# SessionStart -> scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --hook: merges newer saved work, restores Git LFS, re-arms the

    setsid nohup "$REPO/scripts/autosave-cron.sh" "hook:Stop" >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &

    cat > /dev/null 2>&1

    ;;
  *)
    cat > /dev/null 2>&1
    ;;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs headless Blender for Rainbow environment/character work (idempotent).
# Needs network access to download.blender.org (+ apt mirrors for libegl1).
#   bash scripts/setup-blender.sh          -> /opt/blender/blender, symlinked to /usr/local/bin/blender
set -euo pipefail
VER="${BLENDER_VERSION:-5.3.0}"
SERIES="${VER%.*}"
DEST=/opt/blender
if [ ! -x "$DEST/blender" ] || ! "$DEST/blender" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Blender $VER"; then
  tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  curl -sSL -o "$tmp/blender.tar.xz" "https://download.blender.org/release/Blender${SERIES}/blender-${VER}-linux-x64.tar.xz"
  rm -rf "$DEST" && mkdir -p "$DEST"
  tar -xJf "$tmp/blender.tar.xz" -C "$DEST" --strip-components=1
  rm -rf "$tmp"
fi
if ! ldconfig -p | grep -q libEGL.so.1; then
  (apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq libegl1 libsm6 libxi6 libxkbcommon0) > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
ln -sf "$DEST/blender" /usr/local/bin/blender
blender --version | head -1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow (josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-) cloud-environment setup script: paste it into claude.ai ->
# Claude Code -> environment settings -> Setup script. It runs as root before Claude starts, from the folder
# that holds the repository checkout, and installs TOOLS only (npm packages, Python QA libraries, Blender 5.3.0,
# Android SDK 34, World Labs plugin), skipping anything already installed. It never touches git: the
# repository's SessionStart hook (scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --hook) merges newer work, restores Git LFS and
# re-arms the five-minute autosave. Every step is non-fatal so a session always starts.
if [ -f rainbow-/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh ]; then
  bash rainbow-/scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh --env-setup || echo "rainbow: env-setup reported problems"
elif [ -d rainbow- ]; then   # old checkout (e.g. the old default branch) without the bootstrap
  (cd rainbow- && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund > /dev/null 2>&1) || echo "rainbow: npm ci failed"
  (cd rainbow- && bash scripts/setup-blender.sh) || echo "rainbow: blender setup failed"
  (cd rainbow- && bash scripts/setup-android-sdk.sh) || echo "rainbow: android sdk setup failed"
fi
exit 0

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

## 1. Every new session or new Claude account — recovery is automatic

import bpy, sys, os, time, math
out = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1]
def ensure_cam_light(target_objs):
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.camera is None:
        bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0, -6, 2), rotation=(math.radians(75), 0, 0))
        sc.camera = bpy.context.object
        # frame the meshes
        bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
        for o in target_objs: o.select_set(True)
        bpy.ops.view3d.camera_to_view_selected() if bpy.context.area else None
    if not any(o.type == "LIGHT" for o in sc.objects):
        bpy.ops.object.light_add(type="SUN", location=(0, -3, 6)); bpy.context.object.data.energy = 4
def render(blend, name, engine, res=(432, 768), samples=16):
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=blend)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    meshes = [o for o in sc.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
    ensure_cam_light(meshes)
    sc.render.engine = engine
    if engine == "CYCLES":
        sc.cycles.device = "CPU"; sc.cycles.samples = samples; sc.cycles.use_denoising = False
    sc.render.resolution_x, sc.render.resolution_y = res; sc.render.resolution_percentage = 100
    sc.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
    sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(out, f"{name}_{engine}.png")
    t = time.time()
    try:
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
        print(f"RENDER OK  {name} {engine} {res[0]}x{res[1]} in {time.time()-t:.1f}s -> {sc.render.filepath} (camera {sc.camera.name}, {len(meshes)} meshes)")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"RENDER FAIL {name} {engine}: {e}")
root = "/home/user/rainbow-"
render(root + "/qa/pilot05/wave6/camera_lock/screen05_camera_lock.blend", "screen05_camera_lock", "CYCLES")
render(root + "/qa/pilot05/proj/tunnel/lid/lids05.blend", "paddles_lids05", "CYCLES", res=(640, 360), samples=32)
render(root + "/qa/pilot05/wave6/camera_lock/screen05_camera_lock.blend", "screen05_camera_lock", "BLENDER_EEVEE")
# GLB export round-trip of the paddles
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=root + "/qa/pilot05/proj/tunnel/lid/lids05.blend")
glb = os.path.join(out, "lids05_roundtrip.glb")
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=glb, export_format="GLB")
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=glb)
print("GLB ROUNDTRIP OK", os.path.getsize(glb), "bytes,", len([o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]), "meshes:", sorted(o.name for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"))

"""Blender restoration check for the account-transfer session 018Sg3AU (run headless):
    blender -b --factory-startup --python qa/tools_check/blender_transfer_s018/verify_blender.py -- <out_dir>
Checks: bpy, engines (Cycles / EEVEE / Workbench) with a real render each, every tracked .blend opens, the three game GLBs
import (lids05 = six Blender-built gold paddles), and a GLB export -> import round trip that compares the paddle geometry
(vertex / face counts + rounded world-space vertex positions) exactly. Writes results.json next to the renders."""
import bpy, sys, os, json, time, hashlib, subprocess
import numpy as np

ROOT = "/home/user/rainbow-"
out = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
R = {"blender": bpy.app.version_string, "build_date": bpy.app.build_date.decode(), "bpy": True,
     "background": bpy.app.background, "engines": {}, "renders": [], "blends": [], "glbs": {}, "roundtrip": {}}


def mesh_sig(objs):
    """per-mesh (verts, faces, sha of world-space vertex positions rounded to 0.1 mm), sorted by name"""
    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
    sig = {}
    for o in sorted(objs, key=lambda o: o.name):
        ev = o.evaluated_get(dg)
        me = ev.to_mesh()
        co = np.empty(len(me.vertices) * 3, np.float64)
        me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
        co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
        M = np.array(o.matrix_world)
        w = co @ M[:3, :3].T + M[:3, 3]
        w = np.round(w, 4) + 0.0          # +0.0 folds -0.0 into 0.0
        key = np.unique(w, axis=0)        # GLB splits vertices at UV seams: compare the SET of positions
        sig[o.name] = {"verts_unique": int(len(key)), "faces": len(me.polygons),
                       "tris": int(sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in me.polygons)),
                       "bbox_min": [float(x) for x in w.min(0)], "bbox_max": [float(x) for x in w.max(0)],
                       "pos_sha": hashlib.sha256(key.tobytes()).hexdigest()[:16]}
        ev.to_mesh_clear()
    return sig


def img_stats(path):
    px = np.array(bpy.data.images.load(path).pixels[:], np.float32).reshape(-1, 4)
    lum = px[:, :3].mean(1)
    return {"mean": round(float(lum.mean()), 4), "max": round(float(lum.max()), 4), "nonblack_share": round(float((lum > 0.02).mean()), 4)}


# 1. engines available in this build
items = bpy.types.RenderSettings.bl_rna.properties["engine"].enum_items
R["engines"] = {e.identifier: True for e in items}

# 2. real render with each engine: the Blender-built paddles from the game camera (portrait 864x1536 at 50 %)
LIDS = ROOT + "/qa/pilot05/proj/tunnel/lid/lids05.blend"
for eng in ("BLENDER_WORKBENCH", "BLENDER_EEVEE", "CYCLES"):
    if eng not in R["engines"]:
        R["renders"].append({"engine": eng, "ok": False, "error": "engine not in this build"}); continue
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=LIDS)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    cam = bpy.data.objects.get("Cam05_game") or sc.camera
    sc.camera = cam
    sc.render.resolution_x, sc.render.resolution_y, sc.render.resolution_percentage = 864, 1536, 50
    w = bpy.data.worlds.new("qa_world"); sc.world = w; w.use_nodes = True
    bg = w.node_tree.nodes["Background"]; bg.inputs[0].default_value = (1, 1, 1, 1); bg.inputs[1].default_value = 1.2
    sc.render.engine = eng
    if eng == "BLENDER_WORKBENCH":
        sc.display.shading.light = "FLAT"; sc.display.shading.color_type = "TEXTURE"
    if eng == "CYCLES":
        sc.cycles.device = "CPU"; sc.cycles.samples = 16; sc.cycles.use_denoising = False
    if eng == "BLENDER_EEVEE":
        try: sc.eevee.taa_render_samples = 16
        except Exception: pass
    p = os.path.join(out, f"paddles_{eng}.png")
    sc.render.filepath = p; sc.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
    t = time.time()
    try:
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
        st = img_stats(p)
        R["renders"].append({"engine": eng, "ok": os.path.exists(p) and st["nonblack_share"] > 0.01, "seconds": round(time.time() - t, 1),
                             "file": os.path.relpath(p, ROOT), "camera": cam.name if cam else None, **st})
    except Exception as e:
        R["renders"].append({"engine": eng, "ok": False, "error": str(e)[:300]})
    print("RENDER", R["renders"][-1])

# 3. every tracked .blend opens
blends = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "ls-files", "*.blend"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
for rel in blends:
    try:
        bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=os.path.join(ROOT, rel))
        meshes = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
        R["blends"].append({"file": rel, "ok": True, "objects": len(bpy.data.objects), "meshes": len(meshes),
                            "faces": sum(len(o.data.polygons) for o in meshes), "cameras": [o.name for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "CAMERA"]})
    except Exception as e:
        R["blends"].append({"file": rel, "ok": False, "error": str(e)[:300]})
    print("BLEND", R["blends"][-1])

# 4. game GLBs import
for g in ("assets/models/benny.glb", "assets/models/rainbow_girl.glb", "assets/models/lids05.glb"):
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    try:
        bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=os.path.join(ROOT, g))
        meshes = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
        R["glbs"][g] = {"ok": len(meshes) > 0, "meshes": len(meshes), "names": sorted(o.name for o in meshes)[:12],
                        "materials": len(bpy.data.materials), "images": len(bpy.data.images),
                        "armatures": len([o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE"]),
                        "actions": len(bpy.data.actions)}
        if g.endswith("lids05.glb"):

+        R["blends"].append({"file": rel, "ok": False, "error": str(e)[:300]})
+    print("BLEND", R["blends"][-1])
+
+# 4. game GLBs import
+for g in ("assets/models/benny.glb", "assets/models/rainbow_girl.glb", "assets/models/lids05.glb"):
+    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+    try:
+        bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=os.path.join(ROOT, g))
+        meshes = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
+        R["glbs"][g] = {"ok": len(meshes) > 0, "meshes": len(meshes), "names": sorted(o.name for o in meshes)[:12],
+                        "materials": len(bpy.data.materials), "images": len(bpy.data.images),
+                        "armatures": len([o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE"]),
+                        "actions": len(bpy.data.actions)}
+        if g.endswith("lids05.glb"):
+            R["glbs"][g]["paddles"] = mesh_sig(meshes)
+    except Exception as e:
+        R["glbs"][g] = {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:300]}
+    print("GLB", g, {k: v for k, v in R["glbs"][g].items() if k != "paddles"})
+
+# 5. round trip: paddles in lids05.blend -> GLB -> re-import, geometry compared
+bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=LIDS)
+src_meshes = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
+src = mesh_sig(src_meshes)
+glb = os.path.join(out, "lids05_roundtrip.glb")
+bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=glb, export_format="GLB", use_selection=False)
+bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
+bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=glb)
+back = mesh_sig([o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH"])
+game = R["glbs"].get("assets/models/lids05.glb", {}).get("paddles", {})
+same = lambda a, b: {n: (a[n]["pos_sha"] == b.get(n, {}).get("pos_sha") and a[n]["tris"] == b.get(n, {}).get("tris")) for n in a}
+R["roundtrip"] = {"glb_bytes": os.path.getsize(glb), "src_meshes": sorted(src), "back_meshes": sorted(back),
+                  "blend_vs_roundtrip_identical": same(src, back),
+                  "blend_vs_game_glb_identical": same(src, game) if game else "game glb not loaded",
+                  "src": src, "back": back}
+os.remove(glb)    # the round-trip file is a test product, not an asset
+print("ROUNDTRIP", {k: v for k, v in R["roundtrip"].items() if k not in ("src", "back")})
+json.dump(R, open(os.path.join(out, "results.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+print("WROTE", os.path.join(out, "results.json"))

+    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()

+        co = co.reshape(-1, 3)

+        w = co @ M[:3, :3].T + M[:3, 3]
+        w = np.round(w, 4) + 0.0          # +0.0 folds -0.0 into 0.0

def finish(acc, wt, holew, fill_sigma=1.2, along_axis=0, max_gap=400, fill_all=False):
    """normalise; fill tiny gaps by normalised blur; coin holes by linear interpolation along s (axis 0)."""
    img = acc / np.maximum(wt, 1e-9)[..., None]
    valid = wt > 0.2
    hole = holew > np.maximum(wt, 1e-9) * 0.5         # coin pixels dominate this texel
    valid &= ~hole
    blur_w = gaussian_filter(valid.astype(float), fill_sigma)
    blur_c = np.stack([gaussian_filter(np.where(valid, img[..., i], 0), fill_sigma) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
    gap = (~valid) & (blur_w > 0.12) & ~binary_dilation(hole, iterations=1)
    img[gap] = (blur_c / np.maximum(blur_w, 1e-6)[..., None])[gap]
    valid = valid | gap
    # coin holes: interpolate along s (columns), between valid texels at both ends
    hole_t = (binary_dilation(hole, iterations=2) & ~valid | hole) if not fill_all else (~valid | hole)
    Ht, Wt = valid.shape
    filled = np.zeros_like(valid)
    for x in range(Wt):
        col_h = hole_t[:, x]
        if not col_h.any(): continue
        vcol = valid[:, x] & ~col_h
        idx = np.nonzero(vcol)[0]
        if len(idx) < 2: continue
        hy = np.nonzero(col_h)[0]
        lo = np.searchsorted(idx, hy) - 1; hi = lo + 1
        ok = (lo >= 0) & (hi < len(idx))
        hy, lo, hi = hy[ok], lo[ok], hi[ok]
        y0_, y1_ = idx[lo], idx[hi]
        ok = (y1_ - y0_) <= max_gap
        hy, y0_, y1_ = hy[ok], y0_[ok], y1_[ok]
        t = ((hy - y0_) / np.maximum(y1_ - y0_, 1))[:, None]
        img[hy, x] = img[y0_, x] * (1 - t) + img[y1_, x] * t
        filled[hy, x] = True
    # soften the interpolated stripes across u a little
    if filled.any():
        sm = np.stack([gaussian_filter(img[..., i], (0.6, 1.5)) for i in range(img.shape[2])], -1)
        img[filled] = sm[filled]
    valid = valid | filled
    finish.filled = filled
    return img, valid

xE, yE = e_coords(su, ss)
accE, _ = splat(xE, yE, np.where(scoin[:, None], 0, sc), WE, NE)
holeE, _ = splat(xE, yE, scoin[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
wtE, _ = splat(xE, yE, (~scoin)[:, None].astype(float), WE, NE)
E, validE = finish(accE, wtE[..., 0], holeE[..., 0], max_gap=int(NE * 0.35))
alphaE = gaussian_filter(binary_erosion(validE, iterations=1).astype(float), 0.8)
if FARFIX:
    # water the locked eye never saw (behind wave crests, long interpolated runs along s): the straight interpolation
    # shows as a flat blank patch as soon as Benny rides forward. Those texels are released (alpha 0) so the tile
    # layers — the approved design, repeating — show there instead. Runs of <= UNSEEN_MIN rows stay (sub-texel gaps).
    UNSEEN_MIN = 8
    fl = finish.filled.copy()
    run = np.zeros(fl.shape, np.int32)
    for y in range(fl.shape[0]):                       # run length ending at y (down each column)
        run[y] = np.where(fl[y], (run[y - 1] if y else 0) + 1, 0)
    for y in range(fl.shape[0] - 2, -1, -1):           # spread the full run length back up the run
        run[y] = np.where(fl[y] & fl[y + 1], np.maximum(run[y], run[y + 1]), run[y])
    unseen = binary_erosion(run > UNSEEN_MIN, iterations=2)
    alphaE = alphaE * (1.0 - np.clip(gaussian_filter(unseen.astype(float), 1.0) * 1.6, 0, 1))
    print(json.dumps(dict(E_unseen_texels=int(unseen.sum()), E_texels=int(unseen.size))))

if FARFIX:      # N / T / D: water-only samples, as before
    use = use_all
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(use)
    su, ss, sc, scoin = U[use], S[use], tgt[use], coin[use]
# ---------------------------------------------------------------- N (near, full width) layer
sN0, sN1, dN, WN = 126.0, 166.0, 24, 512
NN = int((sN1 - sN0) * dN)
xN = (su + 1) / 2 * WN - 0.5; yN = (ss - sN0) * dN - 0.5

# while riding the coarse old tile shows through them as dark torn stripes across the river. Each gap of <= GAP_MAX
# rows (per column, along s) is filled with the APPROVED texture reflected from both of its edges (above: rows y0,
# y0-1, ...; below: rows y1, y1+1, ...), blended variance-preservingly so the middle keeps the water's contrast — real
# streak detail, continuous at both edges, never a flat interpolated patch. Longer gaps stay to the tile. Texels the
# locked eye saw are untouched (only their soft alpha edge next to a filled gap becomes solid).
GAPFILL = "gapfill" in sys.argv[4:]
if GAPFILL:
    GAP_MAX = 100
    Eg = E.copy(); vg = validE.copy(); n_fill = 0
    for x in range(validE.shape[1]):
        idx = np.nonzero(validE[:, x])[0]
        if len(idx) < 2:
            continue
        for y0, y1 in zip(idx[:-1], idx[1:]):
            g = int(y1 - y0 - 1)
            if g < 1 or g > GAP_MAX:
                continue
            k = np.arange(1, g + 1)
            sa = y0 - (k - 1); sb = y1 + (g - k)
            sa = np.where((sa >= 0) & validE[np.clip(sa, 0, None), x], sa, y0)
            sb = np.where((sb < validE.shape[0]) & validE[np.clip(sb, None, validE.shape[0] - 1), x], sb, y1)
            A = E[sa, x]; B = E[sb, x]
            t = (k / (g + 1.0))[:, None]
            mu = 0.5 * (A.mean(0) + B.mean(0))
            Eg[y0 + k, x] = np.clip(mu + ((1 - t) * (A - mu) + t * (B - mu)) / np.sqrt((1 - t) ** 2 + t ** 2), 0, 1)
            vg[y0 + k, x] = True; n_fill += g
    gf = vg & ~validE                                   # soften across u only inside the filled texels
    sm = np.stack([gaussian_filter(Eg[..., i], (0.5, 1.2)) for i in range(3)], -1)
    Eg[gf] = sm[gf]
    E, validE = Eg, vg
    alphaE = gaussian_filter(binary_erosion(validE, iterations=1).astype(float), 0.8)
    print(json.dumps(dict(E_gapfilled_texels=int(n_fill), E_texels=int(validE.size))))

import numpy as np, json
from PIL import Image
from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter
L=lambda p: np.asarray(Image.open(p).convert('RGB')).astype(float)
def lstd(img, k=9):
    y=img@[0.299,0.587,0.114]; m=uniform_filter(y,k); return np.sqrt(np.maximum(uniform_filter(y*y,k)-m*m,0))
out={}
for d in ('10','20'):
    db0=L('$S/ride_dbg/move_%s.png'%d); db1=L('$O/ride_dbg/move_%s.png'%d); bef=L('$B/move_%s.png'%d); aft=L('$O/ride/move_%s.png'%d)
    water=np.abs(db0-bef).max(-1)>30
    def cls(db):
        r,g=db[...,0],db[...,1]; ratio=g/np.maximum(r+g,1); return ratio
    r0,r1=cls(db0),cls(db1)
    # E-dominated zone of the BEFORE frame, dilated: stripes of tile inside it
    from scipy.ndimage import binary_dilation, binary_closing
    zone=binary_closing(water&(r0>=0.7),iterations=6)&water
    t0=(zone&(r0<0.3)).sum(); t1=(zone&(r1<0.3)).sum()
    out[d]=dict(E_zone_px=int(zone.sum()), tile_stripe_px_before=int(t0), tile_stripe_px_after=int(t1), lstd_zone_before=round(float(lstd(bef)[zone].mean()),1), lstd_zone_after=round(float(lstd(aft)[zone].mean()),1))

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.
